:::{#def-augmented-vector}
#### Augmented vector

The **augmented vector** of $\vx \in \reals^p$
is the vector $\vx^{\mathrm{aug}} \in \reals^{p+1}$
formed by placing a $1$ above the entries of $\vx$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\vx^{\mathrm{aug}}
&= \sbmat{1 \\ \vx} \\
&= \tp{(1, x_1, \ldots, x_p)}
\end{aligned}
$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-augmented-vector}
#### An affine function as a dot product with an augmented vector

For $\vx = \tp{(2, 5)}$, the augmented vector is $\vx^{\mathrm{aug}} = \tp{(1, 2, 5)}$.
With $\vec{w} = \tp{(3, -1)}$ and $b = 4$,
the affine function $\dprod{\vec{w}}{\vx} + b$ (@eq-linear-scalar) equals
the dot product of $\tp{(b, w_1, w_2)} = \tp{(4, 3, -1)}$ with $\vx^{\mathrm{aug}}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\dprod{\vec{w}}{\vx} + b
&= 3 \cd 2 + (-1) \cd 5 + 4 \\
&= 5, \\
\tp{(4, 3, -1)} \cdot \vx^{\mathrm{aug}}
&= 4 \cd 1 + 3 \cd 2 + (-1) \cd 5 \\
&= 5
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
